title: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
blurb: Explain why every PRINCE2 project defines agreed roles that represent business, user and supplier, and builds relationships across its ecosystem.
question: A council wants its IT department's normal line managers to run a new cross-department project, with no separate project roles. Which principle does this neglect?

teach.h: The right people, knowing what is expected
teach.body: Formally: a PRINCE2 project has defined and agreed roles and responsibilities within an organization structure that engages the business, user and supplier interests, and the project management team builds relationships with and between internal and external stakeholders. In plain English: everyone knows their job, all three interests have a voice, and people actively work at getting on with each other.

teach.h: The three interests and who represents them
head: Interest
Concern
Represented on the board by
rows: Uses, operates or is affected by the products
Skills and resources to deliver the products
teach.caption: All three interests must be represented in the project management team; this shapes the project board.

rows.label: Emphasis
values: Who does what AND how people work together

teach.caption: The word 'relationships' is new in v7: building them is part of the principle.

teach.h: Why a project needs its own structure
teach.body: Day-to-day line management structures are often not suited to project work. Projects are cross-functional, may involve several organizations, mix full-time and part-time people, span locations and juggle different priorities. A project structure with agreed roles gives clear accountability and authority, so that people know what is expected of them and what they can expect from others.

teach.caption: The project management team is the three levels inside the project: directing, managing and delivering.

teach.h: Stakeholders inside and outside the business

children.label: Outside the business
children.sub: customers, suppliers, unions, communities, banks, media

teach.caption: The project management team initiates and builds relationships with and between both groups.

teach.body: Ashcombe Borough Council is replacing its parking permit system. Executive Helen Marsh (business) chairs the board; Sam Idowu, head of parking services, is senior user; the software firm's account director, Ravi Shah, is senior supplier. Their role descriptions are drawn up in starting up and confirmed in the project initiation documentation. Project manager Leon Park sets up early meetings between the supplier's developers and the parking wardens who will use the system, and briefs residents' groups. Roles are defined, all three interests are represented, and relationships are being built.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) 'Sponsor' is not a PRINCE2 role; map it to the executive or the business layer. (2) Defining roles is not enough in v7: relationships are part of the principle. (3) Rules still apply when roles are tailored: one executive, and the executive and project manager roles are never combined.

items: Defined and agreed roles and responsibilities within a structure engaging business, user and supplier.
Business = executive; user = senior user(s); supplier = senior supplier(s): all on the project board.
Line management structures are often unsuited to cross-functional project work.
v7 adds relationships: the team builds relationships with and between internal and external stakeholders.

summary: You can now explain the define roles, responsibilities and relationships principle, name which board role represents each of the three interests, and say why v7 added relationships to the principle.

A.q: Which three interests must be represented in a PRINCE2 project management team?
A.why: All projects have three primary stakeholder interests: business, user and supplier, reflected in the project board.

whyNot.1: Finance is not one of the three PRINCE2 interests; its concerns sit within the business interest.
whyNot.2: Customer and regulator are stakeholders, but the three interests are business, user and supplier.
whyNot.3: These are roles and levels, not the three stakeholder interests.

A.q: Which board role represents the supplier interest?
A.why: The senior supplier represents those with the skills and resources to deliver the products.

whyNot.0: The senior user represents the user interest.
whyNot.1: The executive represents the business interest.
whyNot.3: Team managers work at the delivering level and are not board members.

A.q: Why does PRINCE2 set up a project structure rather than relying on line management?
options: Line managers cannot authorize any project spending
Line structures often do not suit cross-functional work
PRINCE2 forbids line managers holding project roles
Project structures replace the organization's hierarchy
A.why: Day-to-day line structures are often not suited to project work, which is cross-functional, may involve several organizations and mixes priorities.

whyNot.0: Spending authority is not the reason; the issue is the structure's fit with project work.
whyNot.2: Line managers can and often do hold project roles such as senior user.
whyNot.3: The project structure is temporary and sits alongside the line hierarchy.

B.q: What did PRINCE2 7 add to the wording of this principle?
B.why: The 6th edition principle was 'defined roles and responsibilities'; PRINCE2 7 adds relationships.

whyNot.0: Accountabilities are covered by roles; the added word is relationships.
whyNot.2: Responsibilities were already part of the 6th edition wording.
whyNot.3: Representation of the three interests was already part of the principle.

B.q:
Which two statements about the define roles, responsibilities and relationships principle are correct?
1. Stakeholders may be inside or outside the business.
2. The principle is satisfied once role descriptions are signed.
3. People should know what they can expect from others.
4. The user interest is represented by the executive.
B.why: Stakeholders can be internal or external (1), and the right people should know what is expected of them and what they can expect from others (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: relationships must also be built throughout the project.
whyNot.1: Both are false: signing roles is not enough, and the executive represents the business interest.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the user interest is represented by the senior user.

B.q: A project manager arranges early workshops between the supplier's developers and the staff who will use the new system. Which principle is this most directly applying?
B.why: Building relationships with and between internal and external stakeholders is part of define roles, responsibilities and relationships.

whyNot.1: The workshops build working relationships; they do not test whether the project is still justified.
whyNot.2: Manage by exception is about tolerances and escalation.
whyNot.3: Manage by stages is about planning and decision points stage by stage.

C.q: Which statement about the executive and the business interest is correct?
options: There may be several executives, one per business area
The executive and project manager roles can be shared
The project manager represents the business interest
One executive represents the business interest
C.why: There is exactly one executive, who represents the business interest on the board and is accountable for the project's success.

whyNot.0: There is only one executive; senior users and senior suppliers can be more than one person.
whyNot.1: The executive and project manager roles cannot be combined.
whyNot.2: The project manager manages day to day; the business interest is represented by the executive.

C.q: Who should the project management team build relationships with, and where are those people found?
options: Board members; inside the project team
Stakeholders; inside and outside the business
C.why: The team initiates and builds relationships with and between internal and external stakeholders, such as users, unions, communities, banks and the media.

whyNot.0: Relationships extend well beyond the board and the project team.
whyNot.2: Suppliers matter, but relationships cover all stakeholders, internal and external.
whyNot.3: Users can be inside or outside the business, and other stakeholders count too.

C.q: A charity names its chief executive as 'project sponsor'. How does this fit the define roles principle?
options: The sponsor is mapped to the executive or business layer
The sponsor replaces the project board for this project
The sponsor becomes the senior user for the project
The sponsor is added as a fourth project board role
C.why: PRINCE2 has no sponsor role; a sponsor may become, or sit above, the executive, so it maps to the executive or the business layer.

whyNot.1: The project board must exist to represent business, user and supplier interests.
whyNot.2: The senior user represents users; a sponsor endorsing the investment fits the business side.
whyNot.3: The board has three roles: executive, senior user and senior supplier.

reteach.title: A wedding needs more than a list of jobs
reteach.question: Picture a wedding where everyone has a job title but nobody talks to the caterer or the venue. What is missing?

blocks.body: A wedding works when the couple (who pay and decide), the guests (who experience it) and the suppliers (venue, caterer) all have a voice, everyone knows their job, and the planner keeps everyone talking. A PRINCE2 project is the same: the business, user and supplier interests are represented, roles and responsibilities are agreed, and the project management team builds relationships between them all.

blocks.text: Agreed role descriptions alone do not satisfy the v7 principle: relationships must be built too.

explain.body: Every project has business, user and supplier interests. All three must be represented in the project management team, which is reflected in the project board.

test.q: Which interest does the senior user represent?
test.why: The senior user represents those who will use, operate, maintain or be affected by the products.

whyNot.0: The executive represents the business interest.
whyNot.1: The senior supplier represents the supplier interest.
whyNot.3: The business layer commissions the project and sits outside the project management team.

explain.body: Roles and responsibilities are defined and agreed so that accountability and authority are clear. Line structures often do not fit project work, so the project has its own structure.

test.q: Why must roles and responsibilities be agreed on a PRINCE2 project?
options: So people know what is expected of them
So the line hierarchy can be replaced
So the business layer can direct the team
So each role is held by a different person
test.why: It is important that the right people are involved and know what is expected of them and what they can expect from others.

whyNot.1: The project structure is temporary and sits alongside the line hierarchy.
whyNot.2: The project board directs the project within the remit set by the business layer.
whyNot.3: Some roles can be combined, for example the PM may also be team manager.

explain.body: The project management team initiates and builds relationships with and between internal and external stakeholders: users, suppliers, unions, communities, banks, the media.

test.q: Which action best shows the 'relationships' part of the principle?
options: Approving the stage plan at a boundary
Setting tolerances for the next stage
Building links with a residents' group
test.why: Building relationships with external stakeholders such as community groups is the relationships part of the principle.

whyNot.0: Approving stage plans is a board decision under manage by stages.
whyNot.1: Setting tolerances applies manage by exception.
whyNot.2: Writing product descriptions applies focus on products.

explain.body: Roles can be tailored (combined, split, added), but some rules hold: one executive; the executive and the project manager are never the same person; project assurance is independent of the project manager.

rows.label: PM also acts as team manager

test.q: Which combination of roles is allowed in PRINCE2?
test.why: Depending on scale and capacity, the project manager may also perform the team manager and project support roles.

whyNot.0: The executive and project manager roles cannot be combined.
whyNot.1: Project assurance cannot be assigned to the project manager.
